title: The Letter to the Romans Timeline
sub: The Righteousness of God · Revealed From Faith to Faith
desc: Paul's most systematic letter, written to a church he'd never visited, building the gospel argument from universal sin through justification by faith, Abraham's example, union with Christ, Israel's place in God's plan, and a long practical close on living sacrificially in community.

eras.label: Era One · Romans 1
eras.name: The Gospel — God's Wrath Against Unrighteousness
eras.dates: Paul's longest, most carefully argued letter opens with a thesis statement and a long list of humanity's suppression of what it already knows about God

events.title: Greeting — Longing to Visit a Church He Never Planted
events.detail: Paul introduces himself at length to a church he did not found and had not yet visited, expressing a long-held desire to come to Rome and preach there too.

verses.text: “I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.”

events.title: The Thesis — ‘The Righteous Will Live by Faith’
events.detail: Two verses state the argument of the entire letter: the gospel is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes, and in it God's righteousness is revealed from faith to faith, exactly as Habakkuk had said centuries earlier.

verses.text: “The righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith; as it is written, ‘But the righteous will live by faith.’” — quoting Habakkuk 2:4.

events.title: Suppressing the Truth — Humanity's Descent Into Idolatry
events.detail: Paul builds his case for universal guilt starting with what all people can see in creation itself — knowledge of God suppressed leads to idolatry, and idolatry to a spiraling list of dishonored relationships and vices.

verses.text: “Since the creation of the world His invisible attributes… have been clearly seen, being understood through what has been made, so that they are without excuse.”

eras.label: Era Two · Romans 2
eras.name: God's Impartial Judgment
eras.dates: Paul turns his indictment on the moral judge who thinks pointing at someone else's sin exempts his own

events.title: You Who Judge Do the Same Things
events.detail: Anyone confident in passing judgment on others is shown to practice the same things themselves — God's kindness is meant to lead to repentance, and his judgment, Paul insists, shows no partiality.

verses.text: “There is no partiality with God.”

events.title: Gentiles With the Law Written on the Heart
events.detail: Gentiles without the Mosaic Law can still show its work written on their conscience — the real division isn't hearing the Law but doing it.

verses.text: “They demonstrate the work of the Law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness.”

events.title: True Circumcision Is of the Heart
events.detail: Paul confronts a Jewish interlocutor directly — boasting in the Law while breaking it dishonors God, and real circumcision, real belonging to the covenant people, is a matter of the heart, not the flesh.

verses.text: “He is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh… circumcision is that which is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter.”

eras.label: Era Three · Romans 3
eras.name: All Have Sinned — Justified by Faith
eras.dates: The verdict on humanity closes, and the gospel's central mechanism — justification by faith apart from the Law — is stated for the first time in full

events.title: Jewish Advantage — Does Unbelief Cancel God's Faithfulness?
events.detail: Paul anticipates an objection: if Israel's unbelief highlights God's faithfulness, is God unjust to judge them? He rejects the logic outright, refusing to let a good outcome justify sin.

verses.text: “If some did not believe, does their unbelief abolish the faithfulness of God? May it never be! Rather, let God be true and every man a liar.”

events.title: None Righteous, Not Even One
events.detail: A dense chain of Old Testament quotations, mostly from the Psalms, builds an airtight case: Jew and Greek alike stand under sin, and the Law's real function was never to justify but to make guilt undeniable.

verses.text: “There is none righteous, not even one; there is none who understands, there is none who seeks for God… there is none who does good, there is not even one.”
“By the works of the Law no flesh will be justified in His sight, for through the Law comes the knowledge of sin.”

events.title: The Righteousness of God Through Faith — A Propitiation in His Blood
events.detail: The letter's theological center: apart from the Law entirely, God's righteousness has been revealed through faith in Christ, who was displayed publicly as the means by which God is both just and the justifier of everyone who believes.

verses.text: “All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, being justified as a gift by His grace through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus.”
“So that He would be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.”

events.title: Boasting Excluded — One God of Jew and Gentile Alike
events.detail: If justification comes by faith rather than works, human boasting has no ground left to stand on — and the one God justifies circumcised and uncircumcised by the very same faith.

verses.text: “We maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the Law.”

eras.label: Era Four · Romans 4
eras.name: Abraham — Justified by Faith, Not Works
eras.dates: Paul reaches back four hundred years before the Law to prove his gospel isn't new, using Israel's own founding father as the pattern

events.title: Abraham Believed God — Counted as Righteousness
events.detail: Abraham had nothing to boast about before God, since Genesis records his righteousness as something counted to him through faith, not earned by works — confirmed by David's own psalm of forgiveness apart from deeds.

verses.text: “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.” — quoting Genesis 15:6.

events.title: Father of All Who Believe — Circumcised or Not
events.detail: Abraham was declared righteous before he was circumcised, not after — making him the father of both uncircumcised believing Gentiles and circumcised believing Jews, on identical terms.

verses.text: “The promise will be guaranteed to all the seed, not only to those who are of the Law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all.”

events.title: Against Hope, In Hope — Written for Our Sake Too
events.detail: Abraham's faith is described in its full absurdity — a hundred-year-old body, a dead womb, believing anyway — and Paul closes by applying the same pattern directly to his readers, whose faith rests on Christ's resurrection.

verses.text: “For our sake also, to whom it will be counted, as those who believe upon Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead, He who was delivered over on account of our transgressions, and was raised on account of our justification.”

eras.label: Era Five · Romans 5
eras.name: Peace With God — Much More
eras.dates: Justification's benefits are named, then the whole human story is compressed into a comparison of two men, Adam and Christ

events.title: Peace With God — Boasting Even in Affliction
events.detail: Justification produces peace with God and access into grace, and Paul traces an unlikely chain: affliction produces perseverance, perseverance produces character, character produces a hope that will not disappoint.

verses.text: “Having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.”

events.title: While We Were Yet Sinners, Christ Died for Us
events.detail: The proof of God's love isn't dying for good people — rare enough on its own — but dying for enemies, while they were still sinners, before any reconciliation had happened at all.

verses.text: “God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.”

events.title: Adam and Christ — Much More Did Grace Abound
events.detail: One man's disobedience brought death to the whole human race; one man's obedience makes righteousness available to everyone who receives it — and wherever sin increased, Paul insists, grace increased even more.

verses.text: “Where sin increased, grace abounded all the more.”

eras.label: Era Six · Romans 6
eras.name: Dead to Sin, Alive to God
eras.dates: An objection anticipated — if grace covers more sin, why not sin more? — answered by baptism's own logic of death and resurrection

events.title: Buried With Him Through Baptism Into Death
events.detail: Baptism is read as a real participation in Christ's death and resurrection — the old self crucified so sin's mastery is broken, and believers are told to consider themselves dead to sin and alive to God.

verses.text: “We were buried with Him through baptism into death, so that as Christ was raised from the dead… so we too might walk in newness of life.”
“Consider yourselves to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.”

events.title: Slaves of Righteousness — The Wages of Sin Is Death
events.detail: Everyone serves a master, Paul argues — formerly slaves of sin, now slaves of righteousness — closing in one of the most quoted verses in the letter, contrasting sin's wage with God's gift.

verses.text: “The wages of sin is death, but the gracious gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

eras.label: Era Seven · Romans 7
eras.name: Released From the Law — The War Within
eras.dates: The Law is defended as holy even while Paul describes, in the most personal terms in the letter, its inability to produce the obedience it demands

events.title: Released From the Law Through Christ's Body
events.detail: A marriage analogy explains the believer's new relationship to the Law — like a widow free to remarry, death (union with Christ's death) has released believers to serve in the new way of the Spirit.

verses.text: “We have been released from the Law, having died to that by which we were constrained, so that we serve in newness of the Spirit and not in oldness of the letter.”

events.title: The Law Is Holy — Sin Used the Commandment
events.detail: Paul defends the Law itself from the charge of being sinful — it exposed coveting he wouldn't otherwise have named, and sin exploited that very commandment to produce death, not the Law's own intent.

verses.text: “The Law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good.”

events.title: Wretched Man That I Am!
events.detail: One of the most personal, debated passages in Paul's letters — a first-person description of wanting to do good and doing evil instead, ending in a cry of anguish answered immediately by thanks through Jesus Christ.

verses.text: “The good that I want, I do not do, but I practice the very evil that I do not want.”
“Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from the body of this death? Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord!”

eras.label: Era Eight · Romans 8
eras.name: No Condemnation — Life in the Spirit
eras.dates: Widely read as the letter's high point — from no condemnation at the start to nothing able to separate believers from God's love at the close

events.title: No Condemnation — The Law of the Spirit of Life
events.detail: Chapter 7's anguish is answered directly: there is now no condemnation for those in Christ, because the Spirit has done what the Law, weakened by the flesh, could never do.

verses.text: “There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.”

events.title: Sons of God — ‘Abba! Father!’
events.detail: Believers led by the Spirit are adopted as God's own children, crying out to him in the same intimate term Jesus himself used — and named co-heirs with Christ, suffering with him now, glorified with him later.

verses.text: “You have received the Spirit of adoption as sons by whom we cry out, ‘Abba! Father!’ The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God.”

events.title: Creation Groans, Waiting for Redemption
events.detail: Present suffering is weighed against a coming glory too large for comparison — all creation itself is pictured groaning like a woman in labor, waiting alongside believers for the redemption of the body.

verses.text: “The whole creation groans and suffers the pains of childbirth together until now.”

events.title: The Spirit Intercedes — All Things Work Together for Good
events.detail: Even prayer itself is carried by the Spirit's own groaning when words fail, leading into an unbroken chain — foreknown, predestined, called, justified, glorified — tracing God's purpose from beginning to end.

verses.text: “We know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to His purpose.”

events.title: Nothing Can Separate Us From the Love of God
events.detail: The chapter closes in a courtroom scene where every possible accuser is silenced, and a sweeping list — death, life, angels, powers, height, depth — is declared powerless to separate believers from Christ's love.

verses.text: “Neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor rulers… will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

eras.label: Era Nine · Romans 9
eras.name: God's Sovereign Choice — Israel's Rejection
eras.dates: Paul turns from personal assurance to national anguish — grief for a people, Israel, who by and large haven't received the gospel he's just described

events.title: Great Sorrow for My Kinsmen According to the Flesh
events.detail: Paul opens the next three chapters with raw emotion — he would trade his own salvation for Israel's, listing every privilege God gave them: adoption, covenants, the Law, the temple, the patriarchs, and Christ himself, by human descent.

verses.text: “I could wish that I myself were accursed, separated from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh.”

events.title: Not All Israel Is Israel — Isaac, Not Ishmael
events.detail: God's word hasn't failed, Paul argues, because physical descent was never the same as the promise — Isaac and Jacob were chosen by God's purpose, not merit, before they had done anything at all.

verses.text: “The children of the flesh are not the children of God, but the children of the promise are considered as seed.”

events.title: The Potter and the Clay
events.detail: One of the most debated passages in the letter, defending God's right to show mercy or harden according to his own purpose — illustrated by Pharaoh and by a potter's authority over the same lump of clay.

verses.text: “Who are you, O man, who answers back to God?… Or does not the potter have authority over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honorable use and another for dishonorable use?”

events.title: A Remnant Will Be Saved — The Stumbling Stone
events.detail: Paul finds his argument already anticipated in Hosea and Isaiah — God calling a people who were not his own, and a remnant preserved out of Israel — while Israel as a whole stumbled over a stone laid deliberately in Zion.

verses.text: “They did not pursue it by faith, but as though it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone.”

eras.label: Era Ten · Romans 10
eras.name: Faith Comes by Hearing
eras.dates: Israel's problem is diagnosed precisely — zeal without knowledge — and answered with a definition of saving faith simple enough for anyone

events.title: Zeal Without Knowledge — Christ Is the End of the Law
events.detail: Israel's zeal for God is real but misdirected, seeking a righteousness of their own rather than submitting to God's righteousness, which finds its goal and endpoint in Christ.

verses.text: “Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.”

events.title: Confess With Your Mouth, Believe in Your Heart
events.detail: One of the most quoted passages on salvation in the whole letter — the word of faith isn't distant or hard to reach, and confession plus belief in Christ's resurrection is available to everyone, Jew or Greek, who calls on his name.

verses.text: “If you confess with your mouth Jesus as Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.”
“Whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”

events.title: Faith Comes From Hearing
events.detail: A chain of questions traces how faith reaches anyone at all — hearing requires a preacher, a preacher requires sending — before Paul shows from Isaiah and Moses that Israel did hear and understand, yet remained a disobedient, obstinate people.

verses.text: “Faith comes from hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Romans 11
eras.name: The Remnant, the Olive Tree, and All Israel
eras.dates: The three-chapter argument about Israel closes with a warning against Gentile arrogance and a doxology too large to summarize

events.title: Has God Rejected His People? A Remnant Chosen by Grace
events.detail: Paul, an Israelite himself, answers his own question emphatically — God has not rejected his people, proven by a present remnant chosen by grace, just as seven thousand remained faithful in Elijah's own despairing moment.

verses.text: “At the present time, a remnant according to God's gracious choice has also come to be.”

events.title: Grafted In — Do Not Boast Against the Branches
events.detail: Israel's stumbling opened the door for Gentile salvation, pictured as a wild olive branch grafted into a cultivated tree — a sharp warning follows against Gentile arrogance, since the natural branches can just as easily be grafted back in.

verses.text: “They were broken off for their unbelief, but you stand by your faith. Do not be haughty, but fear, for if God did not spare the natural branches, He will not spare you, either.”

events.title: The Mystery — And So All Israel Will Be Saved
events.detail: Paul names a mystery he doesn't want his readers ignorant of: a partial hardening on Israel until the full number of Gentiles comes in, and then, he says, all Israel will be saved — one of the most debated promises in the letter.

verses.text: “So all Israel will be saved; just as it is written, ‘The Deliverer will come from Zion, He will remove ungodliness from Jacob.’”
“The gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.”

events.title: Oh, the Depth of the Riches of God's Wisdom
events.detail: Eleven chapters of dense argument end in pure worship — a short, soaring doxology admitting that God's judgments and ways ultimately outrun human comprehension altogether.

verses.text: “Oh, the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments and unfathomable His ways!”
“For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever. Amen.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Romans 12
eras.name: Living Sacrifices — The Body With Many Members
eras.dates: Eleven chapters of doctrine turn, on a single word 'therefore,' into eleven chapters of ordinary Christian living

events.title: Present Your Bodies — Transformed by the Renewing of Your Mind
events.detail: The letter's hinge verse: worship isn't confined to ritual but is a whole life offered as a living sacrifice, with transformation happening through a renewed mind rather than conformity to the surrounding culture.

verses.text: “Present your bodies as a sacrifice—living, holy, and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship. And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.”

events.title: One Body, Many Members, Different Gifts
events.detail: Sober self-assessment, not inflated self-regard, is the starting point for using whatever gift God has given — prophecy, service, teaching, exhortation, giving, leading, mercy — each exercised in its own proportion.

verses.text: “Just as we have many members in one body and all the members do not have the same function, so we, who are many, are one body in Christ.”

events.title: Overcome Evil With Good
events.detail: A rapid-fire list of practical love in action — genuine, hospitable, patient in affliction — climaxing in a refusal to repay evil for evil, choosing instead to overcome evil specifically by doing good.

verses.text: “Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Romans 13
eras.name: Submit to Authority — Put on Christ
eras.dates: Civic obedience grounded in God's own ordering of authority, and an urgent call to wake up before the day arrives

events.title: Every Person Is to Be in Subjection to Governing Authorities
events.detail: One of the New Testament's most direct statements on civic obedience — governing authorities exist under God's own appointment, and resisting them is treated as resisting God's own ordinance.

verses.text: “Every person is to be in subjection to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those which exist have been appointed by God.”

events.title: Love Fulfills the Law — Put on the Lord Jesus Christ
events.detail: Every commandment about how to treat a neighbor is summed up in a single word about love, and Paul closes with urgency — the night is nearly over, so lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on Christ himself like armor.

verses.text: “Love does not work evil against a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the Law.”
“Put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh in regard to its lusts.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Romans 14
eras.name: The Weak and the Strong — Do Not Judge
eras.dates: A disputed question over food and holy days becomes a case study in how believers who disagree should treat one another

events.title: Accept the Weak in Faith — We Will All Stand Before God
events.detail: Disputes over diet and sacred days are treated as matters of personal conviction, not grounds for contempt or judgment — since every believer, strong or weak, answers directly to God, not to one another.

verses.text: “Who are you to judge the servant of another? To his own master he stands or falls; and he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.”

events.title: Do Not Destroy Your Brother Over Food
events.detail: Even where an action is technically permissible, Paul insists love takes priority — the kingdom of God isn't reducible to food and drink, and knowingly causing a weaker believer to stumble is treated as a serious wrong.

verses.text: “The kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · Romans 15
eras.name: Bearing With One Another — Paul's Travel Plans
eras.dates: The practical instructions close, and Paul turns to his own itinerary — Jerusalem first, with an offering, then Rome, then further west to Spain

events.title: Christ Did Not Please Himself — The God of Hope
events.detail: The strong are called to bear the weaknesses of the weak, following Christ's own example of not pleasing himself, and Paul stacks Old Testament citations proving Gentile inclusion in God's praise was always the plan.

verses.text: “May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you will abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.”

events.title: Paul's Ministry Plans — Jerusalem, Rome, and On to Spain
events.detail: Paul explains his missionary strategy of not building on another's foundation, his current mission to deliver a collection to Jerusalem's poor, and his hope to finally reach Rome on his way further west to Spain.

verses.text: “I make it my ambition to proclaim the gospel, not where Christ was already named, so that I would not build on another man's foundation.”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · Romans 16
eras.name: Greetings and a Final Doxology
eras.dates: The longest greeting list in any New Testament letter, including one of only two women in the New Testament called an apostle

events.title: Phoebe, Prisca and Aquila, and Nearly Thirty Names
events.detail: Paul commends Phoebe as a deacon and patron, greets Prisca and Aquila who risked their lives for him, and names nearly two dozen more believers by name — including Junia, described alongside Andronicus as 'outstanding among the apostles.'

verses.text: “Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and my fellow prisoners, who are outstanding to the apostles.”

events.title: A Warning About Those Who Cause Divisions
events.detail: A brief, sharp warning breaks into the greetings — watch for those who cause dissension through smooth, flattering speech — before a promise that the God of peace will soon crush Satan underfoot.

verses.text: “The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet.”

events.title: Closing Greetings — Tertius, the Scribe Who Wrote It Down
events.detail: More names close the letter, including Tertius, the scribe who actually wrote it down as Paul dictated — a rare glimpse of how these letters were physically produced. (The famous closing doxology, ‘to the only wise God be glory forever,’ appears in most Bibles as 16:25-27, but its exact placement varies across ancient manuscripts — some put it here, some after chapter 14, some omit it — and it falls outside the verse numbering this edition’s Greek text uses for chapter 16.)

verses.text: “I, Tertius, who wrote this letter, greet you in the Lord.” — the scribe Paul dictated to, naming himself directly inside the text.
